profile.address: Garden State Parkway, Wall Township, Monmouth County, New Jersey, 08720
profile.reading:
The Manasquan Cable Landing Station sits in Wall Township, Monmouth County, New Jersey, close to the Jersey Shore a few miles inland from Manasquan Inlet. Cable & Wireless USA built the station specifically to land its private Apollo submarine cable system, a transatlantic route connecting the United States to landing points in the United Kingdom and France. When Cable & Wireless's global network assets were folded into Vodafone, ownership of the Manasquan station transferred with them, and Vodafone operates the Apollo system's US landing infrastructure today.

Like other cable landing stations, this building's function is narrow and specific. It terminates the undersea fiber pairs, houses the submarine line terminating equipment and repeater power feed equipment, and connects Apollo's capacity into backhaul networks running toward New York and other inland hubs. It is carrier infrastructure, not a commercial colocation facility, and Vodafone does not publish square footage, power capacity, or customer tenancy figures for it, which is typical across the submarine cable industry.

Wall Township has become something of a cable landing hub in its own right. Tata Communications operates its own landing station in the township, and the NJFX carrier-neutral cable campus sits within a few miles, giving this corner of Monmouth County an unusual concentration of transatlantic connectivity infrastructure for a suburban New Jersey community.

profile.reading:
The Cable & Wireless Cable Landing Station sits at 14 Ramsey Road in Shirley, New York, on the south shore of Long Island in the town of Brookhaven. It was built by Cable & Wireless USA as the landing point for the company's own Apollo submarine cable system, a transatlantic fiber route linking the United States to the United Kingdom and France. Cable & Wireless was later absorbed into Vodafone's global network business, and the Brookhaven station passed to Vodafone along with the rest of the Apollo system's US infrastructure.

Landing stations like this one are carrier facilities rather than commercial data centers. Their job is to bring ashore the fiber pairs of a submarine cable, terminate them in line equipment, and hand traffic off to inland networks, not to host racks of customer servers. Vodafone does not publish square footage, power capacity, or tenancy details for the site, which is standard practice across the submarine cable industry for security and competitive reasons.

The Shirley area is a recognized cluster for transatlantic cable landings. AT&T operates its own Shirley landing station nearby for the TAT-12/13 and AEC-1 systems, and CenturyLink maintains separate stations at Brookhaven for the AC-1 and MAC cables and at Bellport for AC-2/Yellow, making this stretch of Long Island one of the busiest transatlantic cable corridors on the US East Coast.

reading: Vodafone Group is a British multinational telecommunications company with its registered headquarters in Newbury, Berkshire, England. Vodafone owns and operates the Apollo transatlantic submarine cable system, which provides two geographically diverse fiber optic paths across the Atlantic Ocean between the United States and Europe. The facility linked to this operator record, the Manasquan Cable Landing Station tagged here as Apollo, is one of Apollo's US landing points, alongside a separate landing site in Shirley, New York; Apollo's cable segments connect onward to major data center hubs including New York City, Washington DC, and Ashburn, Virginia. This is a distinct facility from the nearby Manasquan TAT-14 cable landing station referenced elsewhere in this registry under the Sprint operator record, since multiple submarine cable systems commonly cluster their US landing points along the same stretch of New Jersey coastline for similar reasons of subsea geography and existing conduit infrastructure. As a cable landing station rather than a general purpose colocation facility, no critical IT megawattage figure was found or would be expected to be published for this Vodafone facility.
